stories.title: Intesa Sanpaolo cuts BlackRock's IBIT stake 94%, triples ether ETF holdings
stories.summary: Italy's largest bank slashed its stake in BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) by 94% during the second quarter while tripling its holdings in an ether ETF, per a filing reported by CoinDesk. The reallocation occurred as crypto prices slumped over the quarter. It offers a concrete look at how a major European bank is repositioning its crypto ETF exposure rather than exiting altogether.
stories.whyItMatters: Large institutional reallocations like this are a real data point on how banks are treating bitcoin versus ether exposure amid price weakness, beyond retail-driven price chatter.
whatToWatch: Whether other banks' filings show a similar bitcoin-to-ether rotation
Intesa Sanpaolo's next quarterly filing for further changes
questions: What drove the rotation into ether over bitcoin specifically?
Is this a tactical trade or a longer-term reallocation?

sources.title: Intesa Sanpaolo slashed IBIT stake by 94% in 2Q, tripled ether ETF holding as crypto prices slumped

stories.title: BlackRock launches tokenized access to $311B of European money market funds
stories.summary: BlackRock has launched tokenized access to money market funds in Europe totaling roughly $311 billion, per CoinDesk, with Cointelegraph reporting the offering is aimed partly at giving stablecoin issuers a tokenized reserve option. It extends BlackRock's tokenization push beyond its existing U.S. BUIDL fund into the European market.
stories.whyItMatters: Tokenized money-market fund access built for stablecoin reserves ties traditional asset management more tightly to crypto market infrastructure, a shift regulators and issuers are watching closely.
whatToWatch: Which stablecoin issuers or crypto firms adopt the tokenized fund access
Whether BlackRock expands the product to other regions
questions: Which specific funds and share classes are being tokenized, and on what infrastructure?

stories.title: Clarity Act stalls in Congress as Warren asks SEC to probe Trump's crypto ties
stories.summary: Market-structure legislation known as the Clarity Act remains stalled amid questions about President Trump's personal crypto business ties, according to CoinDesk. Senator Elizabeth Warren has asked the SEC to investigate Trump over the ethics questions tied up in the bill's delay.
stories.whyItMatters: The Clarity Act is the central bill meant to give the crypto industry regulatory certainty on token classification and market oversight, so its stall directly affects the pace of U.S. crypto regulation.
whatToWatch: The SEC's response to Warren's request
Whether Congress moves the bill forward this session
questions: What exactly is the SEC being asked to investigate, and could it affect the bill's timeline?

stories.whyItMatters: Miners pivoting into AI infrastructure at this scale signals how bitcoin mining economics and AI compute demand are becoming increasingly intertwined, affecting capital allocation across both sectors.

stories.title: Italy's largest bank triples staked ether ETF holdings, cuts IBIT stake
stories.summary: Cointelegraph reports that Italy's biggest bank tripled its holdings in a staked ether ETF while cutting its shares of BlackRock's IBIT bitcoin ETF, based on a regulatory filing. stories.title: Bitcoin nears $64,000 as traders shrug off Strategy's BTC sales, Coldcard sweeps
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded near $64,000, per CoinDesk, with traders apparently looking past reports of BTC sales by Strategy and sweeps of funds from Coldcard hardware wallets. The muted price reaction suggests the market isn't treating either development as a major near-term catalyst.
stories.whyItMatters: The price level marks a notable pullback from prior highs, and traders' apparent indifference to a corporate seller and a hardware-wallet security issue is itself worth tracking for what it implies about current risk appetite.

stories.title: First U.S. spot bitcoin ETF to shut down as inflows dry up
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that the first U.S. spot bitcoin ETF is closing after inflows dwindled, with investors reportedly redirecting money toward AI-focused investments instead. It would mark the first closure among the spot bitcoin ETFs approved in the U.S.
stories.whyItMatters: A spot bitcoin ETF closure this soon after the category's launch is a concrete signal that the field now has more products than sustained investor demand can support.
